questions.q: Why does the storefront-api workflow run test and lint jobs before the build-image job, using `needs: [test, lint]`?
options: GitHub Actions requires jobs to run in alphabetical order
Building a container image costs real CI time, so it's wasteful to build an image for code that fails its quality gates anyway
Docker images cannot be built in the same workflow as tests
needs: has no real effect on job ordering
questions.explain: needs: makes build-image wait until test and lint succeed, avoiding spending expensive build minutes on code that was always going to be rejected.

questions.q: In a multi-stage Dockerfile, why does the final image not include the compilers and build tools used in the `builder` stage?
options: Docker automatically deletes all compilers from any image
Only files explicitly copied via `COPY --from=builder` (or similar) make it into later stages — the builder stage's other contents are discarded
Compilers cannot be installed inside a Dockerfile at all
The final stage always reuses the exact same base image as the builder
questions.explain: Multi-stage builds let later stages selectively copy specific files from earlier stages, leaving everything else (compilers, caches, build tools) behind.

questions.q: Why does storefront-api's build step tag its image with `${{ github.sha }}` instead of only `latest`?
options: github.sha makes the build run faster
It gives every image an immutable, traceable identity — the tag itself identifies exactly which commit produced it
latest tags are not supported by container registries
SHA tags are required for Kubernetes to pull an image
questions.explain: Tagging by commit SHA means there's never ambiguity about which source code produced a given image, unlike a mutable tag like latest.

questions.q: What is the practical risk of deploying production from an image tagged only `latest`?
options: latest images are always larger in file size
latest is a mutable pointer that can be overwritten by a newer build, so it doesn't reliably identify which code is actually running
latest images cannot be pulled by Kubernetes
There is no risk; latest is the recommended production tag
questions.explain: Because latest gets reassigned to whatever was built most recently, it doesn't give a reliable, traceable record of which commit is deployed.

questions.q: After storefront-api's image is built and pushed, where does it show up for the repository?
options: Only in the local Docker daemon that built it
In GitHub's Packages feature, visible in the repository's own sidebar
It is automatically emailed to the development team
It is deleted automatically after the workflow completes
questions.explain: Once pushed, the image lands in the repository's Packages section, which lists every package (including container images) published from that repo.
